To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
albumin substitution in patients with ascites undergoing large volume paraccentesis does not improve mortality.
albumin infusion does not improve mortality in patients with large volume paracenteses.
the administration of albumin does not reduce the mortality in HCC‐ free cirrhotic subjects who undergo large volume paracenteses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of albumin on the mortality and morbidity of patients with liver cirrhosis undergoing large volume paracenteresis.
the effects of albumin infusion on mortality and morbility of patients who underwent large volume paracentesia.
the following questions: 1) Is the infusion of albumin after large‐volume paracentesis associated with a reduction of mortality in patients with cirrhosis?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is insufficient evidence of benefit regarding survival due to albumin infusion in patients undergoing large volume therapeutic paracentesis.
the evidence is insufficient to support albumin administration in HCC‐ free cirrhotic subjects undergoing large volume paracentsis.

albumin infusion is beneficial in terms of mortality and morbidity reduction after large volume parcentesis in cirrhotic non‐hepatocellular carcinoma patients, but this benefit has not been demonstrated for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is insufficient evidence to support the use of albumin in HCC‐ free cirrhotic subjects who undergo large volume paracenteses.
there is insufficient evidence to support albumin substitution in the context of cirrhotic ascites undergoing large volume paracentsis.

the use of human albumin is not associated with a reduction of mortality in cirrhotic HCC‐free patients who undergo a large volume paracenteses, but may be associated with a reduction in the risk of developing renal failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is insufficient evidence of benefit of albumin infusion in HCC‐ free cirrhotic patient undergoing large volume paracentsis in order to reduce mortality.
the evidence supporting the recommendation for the infusion of human serum albumin is not robust and further research is warranted.
there is currently insufficient evidence of benefit regarding the mortality due to albuminus infusion in patients undergoing large volume (5–6 L) paracentesis.
